masked.report: June 21, 2022 Pipeline/Haywire Fire Daily Update (covers June 20)
masked.quote: Yesterday, crews took advantage of the conditions and performed tactical firing operations in the northeast edge to tie the fire's edge into the Tunnel Fire burn scar to secure the outer edge of the fire.
masked.reason: the only perimeter-changing activity reported for the period; the same reports describe only interior heat and smoke otherwise (plainly implies the period's growth is from firing). Growth in the period is small (26,528 acres on June 20) and the interval is probably outside the evaluation window (90 % of the final area is reached by about June 16)

candidates_not_masked.text: Burning operations on the northeast edge of the fire helped reduce available fuels.
candidates_not_masked.reason: one activity among line construction and aerial suppression; growth not attributed to it ('constructed firelines held with little growth')

candidates_not_masked.text: Burning operations on the northeast edge of the fire helped reduce available fuels. Fire growth was mostly along the eastern edge toward the Tunnel Fire burn area.
candidates_not_masked.reason: growth is located, not attributed to the burning operations

candidates_not_masked.text: initial attack groups stand ready to quickly respond to any spotting over the line

pipeline.note: Window start 2022-06-14 04:44 UTC (first NIROPS scan). The June 13 and June 15 reports attribute growth to strong winds and contain no firing or spotting terms.
